author: curriculum-architect
songSummary: Practices call and answer, counted silences, walk and run-ning notes, and low left-hand notes, with Mozart's bright serenade for strings.

classes.title: The rocket call
classes.goal: Find G, then learn the opening call that climbs by skips.

mathTarget.parentLine: The opening skips up the keys like a rocket

classes.parentPrompt: Help your child find G first, then point to the D below it.
classes.childAction: Find G, then play the call: G, D, G, D.
classes.bridge: G sits between the first two of the three black keys; the call starts there.

intro.caption: Let's find the rocket's launch pad
intro.parentCue: help your child find G by the three black keys.

games.caption: The call: G, D, G, D
games.parentCue: Say the fingers: four, one, four, one

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: finding G and playing the opening call.

classes.title: Rocket up, parachute down
classes.goal: Learn the answer and hear it fall the way the call rose.

mathTarget.parentLine: The call climbs up high; the answer climbs back down low

classes.parentPrompt: Lift your arm on the call, lower it on the answer; let your child copy.
classes.childAction: Play the answer and hear it fall the way the call rose.
classes.bridge: The call is a rocket going up; the answer is a parachute floating down.

intro.caption: Up goes the rocket
intro.parentCue: lift your arm high, then float it down.

games.caption: The call goes up, the answer comes down
games.parentCue: Lift your arm, then float it down

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: hearing a call and its mirror answer.

classes.title: Call, answer, then the tune
classes.goal: Play the whole piece slowly, all parts in order.

mathTarget.parentLine: Two calls first, then a singing tune: three parts in order

classes.parentPrompt: Name each part as it starts: call, answer, tune. Hum it if your child stalls.
classes.childAction: Play the parts in order: call, answer, then the tune.
classes.bridge: The piece calls twice, like knocking, then opens the door to a singing tune.

intro.caption: Three parts, in order
intro.parentCue: name each part as it starts.

games.caption: Tap the beat: the first line
games.parentCue: Play the blue keys; your child taps the beat

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: playing the parts of a piece in order.

classes.title: G, shh, D
classes.goal: Practise the call with its tiny silences, slowly, then a little faster.

mathTarget.parentLine: A silence is part of the music; we count it too

classes.parentPrompt: Whisper 'shh' on each rest; your child lifts the finger, then plays D.
classes.childAction: Play G, lift your finger for the 'shh', then play D.
classes.bridge: A rest is a held breath: the hand floats up, then lands.

games.caption: G, shh, D. G, shh, D.

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: counting silences inside the music.

classes.title: The low cello note
classes.goal: Play one low left-hand note at the start of each bar.

mathTarget.parentLine: The left hand plays low notes, on the left side

classes.parentPrompt: Play the tune; count bars aloud so your child plays one low note each.
classes.childAction: Play one low note with your left hand on each 'one'.
classes.bridge: The left hand is a big cello on the left: one deep note per bar.

intro.caption: The low cello note
intro.parentCue: count one at each new bar

games.caption: Same G, lower house
games.parentCue: Ask: which G sounds like a cello?

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: low notes with the left hand.

classes.title: Two hands land on one
classes.goal: Play the tune with one low left-hand note on each bar, very slowly.

mathTarget.parentLine: Each hand has its own job; they meet on the 'one'

classes.parentPrompt: Go very slowly; say 'one' each time both hands play together.
classes.childAction: Left hand on 'one', right hand plays the tune, slowly.
classes.bridge: Both hands land together on 'one', like two feet jumping.

intro.caption: Two hands, two jobs
intro.parentCue: go very slowly and stop while it's fun.

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: giving each hand its own job.

classes.title: Walk, walk, run-ning
classes.goal: Play both hands a bit faster, feeling walking notes and running notes.

mathTarget.parentLine: Two running notes fit in the time of one walking note

classes.parentPrompt: Say 'walk, walk, run-ning, run-ning' as your child plays a bit faster.
classes.childAction: Walk notes are long, run-ning notes are quick. A bit faster!
classes.bridge: Two running notes fit into one walking step.

intro.caption: Walk, walk, run-ning, run-ning
intro.parentCue: say it aloud as your child plays.

games.caption: Walk, walk, run-ning, run-ning
games.parentCue: Clap the walks and run-nings together

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: walking notes and running notes, half and double.

classes.title: Play with Mozart's strings
classes.goal: Play the whole piece along with the music at full speed.

mathTarget.parentLine: Keeping your part going while the music moves on

classes.parentPrompt: Sit close and nod the beat; if a note is missed, keep going.
classes.childAction: Play along with the music. Missed notes are fine; keep going!
classes.bridge: The music is a string orchestra; you are one more player in it.

intro.caption: Join the string orchestra
intro.parentCue: nod the beat and keep going, whatever happens.

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: keeping up with the music, together.

classes.title: Night music for teddy
classes.goal: Play the whole piece for teddy: bold calls, gentle tune.

mathTarget.parentLine: Playing the calls bold and bright, the tune gentle

classes.parentPrompt: Sit teddy as the audience; play the calls bold, the tune gentle, then bow.
classes.childAction: Play the calls bold and the tune gentle for teddy.
classes.bridge: The calls are bold and bright; the tune sings softly, like the night.

intro.caption: Concert time for teddy!
intro.parentCue: put teddy in front as the audience.

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: bold and gentle playing, start to end.
